features.feature_value: Graphic language was considered unacceptable even if context might justify it
features.evidence_span: The graphic language used was not acceptable even though the context may have been
features.rationale: The participant explicitly links disapproval to the presence of graphic/inappropriate language when making keep/remove decisions.

features.feature_value: They judged whether language felt incendiary; profanity ok but not if it attacks a person
features.evidence_span: Profanity is acceptable but not attacking another person.
features.rationale: They articulate a specific rule distinguishing acceptable profanity from unacceptable personal attacks based on incendiary/targeted intent.

features.feature_value: Cursing was the main influencer; free speech is supported but norms should restrict cursing
features.evidence_span: the only thing that majorly influenced my decision was the posts with a lot of cursing....we do have freedom of speech...but the norms are to not allow the cursing.
features.rationale: They clearly name cursing as the dominant decision driver and explicitly balance it against free speech norms.

features.feature_value: Disliked cursing on public platforms because kids might read them
features.evidence_span: I just don't agree with the cursing on public platforms where kids might be reading
features.rationale: They justify removal/negative evaluation via audience/children exposure rather than threat-to-safety.

features.feature_value: Direct attacks were moderated; expletives reviewed but not auto-removed
features.evidence_span: directly attacked another were moderated. Posts with explitives were reviewed but not automatically removed.
features.rationale: They describe a conditional policy-like process distinguishing attacks vs profanity for removal decisions.

features.feature_value: Harsh/aggressive language was accepted because no specific calls for violence or threats were made
features.evidence_span: none outright called specifically for violence... Since no threats were made, each pairing was protected by freedom of speech and I chose to accept them all.
features.rationale: Their keep decision is explicitly tied to absence of violence threats/calls for violence.

features.feature_value: Aimed to keep expression while removing hateful and violent language
features.evidence_span: support freedom of expression, while removing hateful and violent language.
features.rationale: They state a dual-purpose rule that directly governs which content gets removed.

features.feature_value: Free speech is broad; line crossed when genuine disinformation spreads on serious topics
features.evidence_span: The line is crossed when genuine disinformation is being spread about serious topics.
features.rationale: They specify a concrete threshold (genuine disinformation) as the point where they would diverge from free-speech acceptance.
